headline: Loonie jumps on strong retail sales; bitcoin steady near $81,700 before the open
summary: U.S. stocks are set to open slightly lower after Thursday's tech rout (Nasdaq down 2.6%, S&P 500 down 1.2%): S&P futures are off about 0.2% and Dow futures about 0.5% as telecoms sink on a SpaceX wireless report, while American Express slips despite beating forecasts. In Canada, August retail sales rose 1.2% and the loonie jumped about 0.5% to 71.6 U.S. cents, a one-month high, as traders put roughly 80% odds on a Bank of Canada rate hike on Wednesday. Bitcoin is flat near $81,700 and ether near $2,400, with Fear & Greed at 50 (Neutral); PEPE, AKEDO and Bitcoin Cash lead a small altcoin bounce, U.S. crude is up 2.3% to about $101.80 and the 10-year yield is near 4.97%.

crypto.label: Cautious
crypto.why: Bitcoin and ether are flat in a tight range and a few altcoins are bouncing, but spot bitcoin ETFs just had their biggest outflow since June and the Fear & Greed index fell from 68 (Greed) to 50 (Neutral) in a day.

stocks.label: Cautious
stocks.why: Futures point to a slightly lower open after the Nasdaq's worst day since June, the VIX fear gauge is up near 20, and oil above $100 keeps inflation and rate-hike worries alive ahead of next week's Fed and Bank of Canada decisions.

drivers.title: AI-spending doubts hit Big Tech and chips
drivers.detail: Meta closed down 7% at $648.85 Thursday even after beating forecasts, as investors weigh its $135–$145 billion spending plan and negative free cash flow; AMD fell 8.1%, Amazon 4.6%, and Nvidia and Broadcom about 4.3–4.4%. Nasdaq 100 futures are roughly flat early Friday, and investors are now looking to Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon results next week for proof the spending pays off.
drivers.assets: Nasdaq, chip stocks, Shopify, Celestica, bitcoin

drivers.title: Bond yields steady after big drop
drivers.detail: The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 19 basis points (0.19 percentage point) Thursday to about 4.95%, its biggest one-day drop since March 2023, and is edging back up to about 4.97% early Friday. The Fed is expected to hold at 3.75%–4.00% on Oct. 28, but traders still see a December rate hike as likely.

drivers.title: Brent hits five-month high near $114
drivers.detail: Brent crude is near $114 a barrel, its highest in more than five months, and U.S. crude is up about 2.3% to $101.80, after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites and reports of possible renewed U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran. Higher oil feeds inflation fears ahead of next week's central bank meetings and supports Canadian energy producers, while gold is down about 0.4% near $4,045.
drivers.assets: Oil, Canadian energy stocks, bonds, crypto

drivers.title: SpaceX wireless report hits U.S. telecoms
drivers.detail: AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile are each down more than 3% premarket after a report that SpaceX is in talks with cell-tower companies about a nationwide wireless carrier program. Tower owners jumped instead, with Crown Castle up about 8.5% and American Tower about 5.6%, which is dragging Dow futures down about 0.6%.

drivers.title: Bitcoin ETFs post biggest outflow since June
drivers.detail: Spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold real bitcoin) took in about $1.08 billion over the prior three days, then lost about $635 million on Thursday, the largest one-day outflow since June 25 per SoSoValue data, while ether funds have lost more than $1 billion this month. About $406 million of leveraged crypto bets were wiped out over 24 hours, per CoinGlass.

drivers.title: Bank of Canada rate hike now likely
drivers.detail: August retail sales rose 1.2% (1.2% excluding autos too), and Statistics Canada's early estimate shows another 0.7% gain in September, after Governor Tiff Macklem warned high oil prices will push inflation forecasts up; swap markets price about 80% odds of a hike to 2.50% on Oct. 28, up from roughly 30% a week ago. The loonie rose about 0.5% to 71.6 U.S. cents, a one-month high, which helps Canadians buying U.S. assets but raises borrowing-cost worries for mortgage holders and rate-sensitive stocks.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Flat over 24h and down 1.1% this week, at about $81,770 (down 4.6% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin climbed to nearly $85,000 late Wednesday, briefly breaking above the $84,000 ceiling that had stopped it on Oct. 13–14, then fell back below $82,000 overnight as Tesla's and Meta's results revived doubts about AI spending; it held near $81,000–$81,700 as the Nasdaq closed down 2.6%. The round trip caused about $458 million of liquidations over the day (leveraged bets closed automatically), about 91% of them bullish bets, per CoinGlass data cited by The Crypto Times. Bitcoin's share of total crypto value is near 59.5%, close to its highest since May, as traders shelter in it while smaller coins fall harder. Overnight it dipped to about $81,000 and by 9:30 a.m. Friday was near $81,700, a range of less than $1,000 and still below the $82,500 level it lost Thursday; SoSoValue data show spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $635 million on Thursday, their biggest single-day outflow since June 25, ending three days of inflows worth about $1.08 billion.
crypto.meaning: Bitcoin is now trading closely with tech stocks, and it is sitting just above the $80,000 floor of the $80,000–$87,000 range it has held for a month. ETF buying helps, but it is below the pace that came with past strong rallies, and some traders warn that a clean break below about $80,000 could open a slide toward $75,000 or lower.

outlook.bullCase: Reclaiming $84,000–$85,000 with steady ETF inflows and a firmer Nasdaq could carry it to the top of the range near $87,000–$87,500; a break above that would be a bigger shift.
outlook.bearCase: A further slide in tech stocks, a hawkish Fed on Oct. 28, or higher oil could push it below the $80,000 floor, with some traders eyeing $75,000–$70,000 if that gives way.
outlook.watch: Whether the Nasdaq steadies after today's open, the $80,000 and $85,000 levels, whether Thursday's large ETF outflows continue, and the Fed decision on Oct. 28.

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Up 0.1% in 24h, down 3% this week, at about $2,404 (down 12% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ether briefly rose to about $2,490 with bitcoin on Wednesday, then gave the gain back and is hovering right around the $2,400 level that had held as support for about a week, after dipping under it Thursday. It keeps trailing bitcoin as U.S. ether ETFs kept losing money: about $26 million on Tuesday and an estimated $31 million more on Wednesday, taking October outflows past $1 billion, the worst month of 2026. On the plus side, a record 43.8 million ETH (about 36% of supply) is staked, meaning locked up to secure the network. Separately, CoinDesk reports developers postponed a test of the next upgrade, Glamsterdam, after security researchers flagged a risk to existing smart contracts, a reminder the upgrade's timing could slip.
crypto.meaning: Ether is lagging bitcoin because big investors keep pulling money from the ETFs. Until those flows turn, rallies may be harder to sustain.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above $2,400, ETF outflows stopping and a firm hold above $2,500 could open a move toward about $2,700, where October began.
outlook.bearCase: Staying below $2,400 with continued ETF outflows could send it toward the $2,300 area, and a broader risk-off turn could push it lower.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the $2,400 and $2,500 levels, the ETH/BTC ratio, and any new Glamsterdam upgrade timeline.

crypto.name: Pepe
crypto.move: Up 12% in 24h and 23% this week, at about $0.00000504 (up 7% over 30 days); trending on CoinGecko
crypto.why: PEPE, the largest frog-themed meme coin (a token with no product, driven by online hype), is the biggest gainer among large coins today. There is no official news behind it: on Oct. 21 it had the biggest jump in trading activity on South Korean exchanges relative to normal, and futures trading has been running at more than five times spot trading, with open interest (the value of open bets) near $270 million, per CoinMarketCap's summary of market data. Early Friday CoinDesk flagged it up about 13% as smaller coins bounced while bitcoin held steady.
crypto.meaning: Gains built on borrowed money and a burst of retail trading in one region can unwind fast if those bets are closed. PEPE is still far below its December 2024 record, and meme coins tend to swing much more than bitcoin in both directions.

outlook.bullCase: If meme-coin interest keeps building and bitcoin holds $80,000, PEPE could extend toward the $0.0000055–$0.000006 area.
outlook.bearCase: A wider crypto sell-off or a wave of liquidations (leveraged bets closed automatically) could erase the week's gain and send it back toward $0.0000041–$0.0000044.
outlook.watch: Futures open interest and funding rates, Korean exchange volume, and whether bitcoin holds $80,000.

crypto.name: AKEDO
crypto.move: Up 25% in 24h and 18% this week, at about $0.0348 (down 29% over 30 days)
crypto.why: AKEDO is a small AI-tools token that has just squeezed into CoinGecko's top 100. We could not find a clear news catalyst for the jump, which peaked overnight near $0.037, dropped about 14% in one hour before 3:30 a.m., and has since bounced back to about $0.035; it comes two days after a scheduled Oct. 21 unlock of tokens worth about $63 million (roughly 9% of its market value), and after weeks stuck in a $0.029–$0.037 range. Earlier community analysis found the top 100 wallets hold almost all of the supply, so a few holders can move the price sharply.
crypto.meaning: A double-digit jump on no identifiable news, in a token with extremely concentrated ownership, is the kind of move that can reverse just as quickly. The price was turned back at the old $0.037 ceiling, and anyone holding it is exposed to large holders and fresh unlocked supply.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above the old $0.037 ceiling on steady volume would turn that level into support and could extend the move.
outlook.bearCase: Selling by large holders or recipients of the Oct. 21 unlock could send it back into the $0.029–$0.03 range or toward about $0.022, a level flagged as key support.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds above about $0.03, trading volume, large-wallet transfers to exchanges, and any official project news.

crypto.name: Quant
crypto.move: Down 6.2% in 24h and 13% this week, at about $182 (still up 147% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Quant makes software (Overledger) that connects banks' systems to blockchains. Its token soared after The Clearing House, a group owned by large U.S. banks, picked Quant on Sept. 24 to link systems for its plan to put bank deposits on blockchains. Since then it has been giving back gains through profit-taking and heavy leverage: it fell about 19% in the week to Oct. 20 and is sliding again with the altcoin sell-off.
crypto.meaning: The bank deal adds credibility, but it does not require banks to buy or hold the QNT token itself, so the price may have run ahead of what the deal means for token demand. After a gain this large, sharp swings in both directions are likely.

outlook.bullCase: Holding the $170–$200 support zone and new details on bank pilots could bring a rebound toward $220–$250.
outlook.bearCase: A clean break below about $170 could extend the pullback toward $140–$150 as late buyers sell.
outlook.watch: The $170 level, futures open interest, and any updates from The Clearing House or Quant on the deposit-token project.

crypto.name: Bitcoin Cash
crypto.move: Up 3.6% in 24h and 0.9% this week, at about $285 (down 18% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin Cash, a 2017 offshoot of bitcoin built for cheaper payments, is one of the few large coins rising today. The main story is CME Group, the big U.S. futures exchange, which began listing regulated, cash-settled BCH futures on Oct. 19 (a full contract covers 250 BCH, a micro contract 25), and confirmed the first large block trade between trading firms FalconX and GSR on Oct. 20. Futures let bigger institutions bet on or hedge BCH without holding the coin.
crypto.meaning: New regulated products can bring in larger traders, but this has been tried before: when CME announced the contracts on Sept. 22, BCH ran from the $260s to above $360 and then gave most of it back, so the listing alone has not been enough to hold gains.

outlook.bullCase: A daily close above its 200-day average near $291 and then the $300–$310 resistance zone could open a move back toward the September highs around $358–$360.
outlook.bearCase: If bitcoin weakens, BCH could slip back to support at $264–$279; a close below about $264 would put the $215–$225 area in view.
outlook.watch: CME BCH futures volume and open interest, the $291 and $264 levels, bitcoin's hold of $80,000 and the Oct. 28 Fed decision.

crypto.name: Lighter
crypto.move: Down 9.4% in 24h but up 8% this week, at about $3.34 (down 35% over 30 days)
crypto.why: The token of the Lighter derivatives exchange jumped after reports from its Oct. 21 investor call that it plans to apply for a U.S. licence in November and is weighing access through Robinhood's U.S. platform; neither has been confirmed. crypto.meaning: The move rests on unconfirmed plans. Only 25% of the 1 billion tokens are circulating, so future supply is a long-term overhang, and the token is still about half its all-time high.

outlook.bullCase: An official licence filing or Robinhood announcement could push it toward the $4.50–$5 area.
outlook.bearCase: No confirmation, or more profit-taking after Wednesday's 20% jump, could send it back toward about $3.20 or below.
outlook.watch: Official statements from Lighter, trading volume versus Hyperliquid, and token unlock schedules.

crypto.name: Monero
crypto.move: Down 2.8% in 24h but up 8.1% this week, at about $610 (up 8% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Monero, a privacy-focused coin that hides who sends what, has slipped from about $650 late Wednesday to near $611, down about 4% over 24 hours early Friday, one of the bigger drops among large coins over the past day, though it is still up about 9% on the week. We found no project-specific news behind the pullback (the latest software release on Oct. 16 was routine maintenance), so it looks like the crowded leveraged trade unwinding as the wider market cooled. The run had started after veteran chart trader Peter Brandt called XMR his favourite large-cap setup, and futures trading had outpaced spot (actual coin) trading, with funding rates (the fee bullish leveraged traders pay to keep bets open) near 70% a year, per CoinDesk.
crypto.meaning: Rallies driven by borrowed money can reverse quickly if traders are forced to close positions (a liquidation). Monero is also still about 18% below its January record near $799, and an EU anti-money-laundering rule from July 2027 will bar regulated crypto firms from handling privacy coins, which limits where it can trade.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above the old $600 resistance could keep momentum going toward the $700 area and, beyond that, the January high near $799.
outlook.bearCase: A leverage flush could drag it back through $600 toward the $520–$560 zone where it bounced earlier this month.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds the $600 line, futures open interest and funding rates (falling funding would mean the leverage is clearing out), spot versus futures volume, and any exchange delisting news.

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Down 0.9% in 24h and flat this week, at about $1,231 (down 24% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Traders had been positioning for the NU7 upgrade, which developers scheduled for about 7:50 p.m. ET on Nov. 5; it cuts block times from 75 to 25 seconds and sends 60% of fees to a reserve. Futures open interest (the value of open bets) had risen about 19–24% and two large traders reportedly opened about $37.6 million of 10x leveraged longs. Those leveraged bets have been unwinding: CoinDesk flagged ZEC among the coins where bullish traders were closing positions, and the price has dropped back to just above the $1,190–$1,230 support area, where it is holding today.
crypto.meaning: Much of this month's rally was driven by borrowed money, and today shows how fast that can reverse. Upgrade dates often bring 'buy the rumour, sell the news' behaviour, so swings both ways are likely into Nov. 5.

outlook.bullCase: Holding the $1,180–$1,200 area and renewed interest as the upgrade nears could bring it back to the $1,375 resistance and, beyond that, the September high near $1,700.
outlook.bearCase: Losing $1,180 would erase the October breakout and could send it toward about $1,000–$1,120, near its 50-day average.
outlook.watch: The $1,180 level, funding rates and open interest, ETF flows, and any upgrade delay.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Flat over 24h, down 2% this week, at about $104.40 (down 11% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Solana completed its Alpenglow upgrade, a major overhaul aimed at much faster transaction finality (the point at which a payment can't be reversed), according to CoinDesk. The price has moved with the market rather than rallying on the news, and it is roughly flat over the past day near $104.
crypto.meaning: A smooth Alpenglow launch is a meaningful technical milestone, but the market is treating it as already expected. The first days after a big upgrade are when problems usually show up, so stability matters more than headlines.

outlook.bullCase: A trouble-free upgrade and stronger crypto risk appetite could lift SOL back toward $115–$120.
outlook.bearCase: Any outage or bug after the upgrade, or a bitcoin break below $80,000, could push SOL under $100.
outlook.watch: Network stability after Alpenglow, bitcoin's $80,000–$85,000 range, and Solana ETF flows.

stocks.name: S&P 500
stocks.move: Closed down 1.2% at 7,663 Thursday, about 2.3% below its record near 7,845; futures down about 0.2% before Friday's open
stocks.why: The index slid through the session as Meta, AMD, Amazon and Nvidia fell on renewed doubts about returns from AI spending, while oil near $100 revived inflation worries. Apple (up 1.2% to a record) and JPMorgan (up 0.4%) cushioned the drop, the Dow ended flat, and the VIX fear gauge rose about 14% to 19.
stocks.meaning: The damage is concentrated in tech, which makes up a large share of the index, while other sectors are holding up better. Falling bond yields help a little, but a 10-year yield near 5% still makes stocks look expensive relative to bonds.

outlook.bullCase: Solid results from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon next week, a calm Fed on Oct. 28 and yields easing further could carry it back toward the 7,845 record.
outlook.bearCase: A deeper tech sell-off, a hawkish Fed, or an oil spike above $115 could drag it below 7,600 toward the 7,500 area.
outlook.watch: Whether the 7,600 area holds Friday; oil prices, and the Fed decision on Oct. 28 followed by Microsoft and Alphabet earnings that evening.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.move: Closed down 7% at $648.85 Thursday after touching $639.69; down about 0.6% more in premarket trading Friday
stocks.why: Third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, beating forecasts, and fourth-quarter guidance topped estimates, but the stock fell as investors focus on costs: Meta expects $135–$145 billion of capital spending, free cash flow was about -$2.1 billion this quarter, and a $9.9 billion legal charge cut reported profit. It also surprised Wall Street with a new non-voting Class C share, one for every share held starting in January 2027; JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth called the pending shares an overhang (a supply worry hanging over the price) and urged Meta to issue any new stock quickly. Meta's filing says the Class C dividend is expected to work like a two-for-one stock split for Class A holders.
stocks.meaning: The core ad business is growing fast, which supports the stock, but AI spending pushed free cash flow negative (about -$2.1 billion) this quarter. A separate $25 billion penalty imposed by a New Mexico judge in a privacy case is under appeal and adds legal uncertainty.

outlook.bullCase: At least 13 brokerages raised price targets after the results, per LSEG; if buyers return to the strong ad growth, it could recover toward the $700 level.
outlook.bearCase: Worry about open-ended AI spending, a share sale to fund it, or the $25 billion New Mexico penalty could push it below Thursday's low near $640 toward the $620–$630 area.
outlook.watch: Whether Thursday's low near $640 holds, any details on Class C share issuance, and Alphabet's and Microsoft's spending plans on Oct. 28.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.move: Closed down 8.1% at $507.93 Thursday, about 23% below its 52-week high; up nearly 1% premarket Friday
stocks.why: There is no AMD-specific news; it is falling in a broad AI-chip sell-off as Meta's spending plans and a report that Nvidia and Tesla will invest $2.8 billion in Samsung Electro-Mechanics revived worries about 'circular' financing, where chip buyers and sellers fund each other. Intel is down 4–5%, Nvidia about 4.4%, and Lam Research about 9% after its own results. AMD also trades at a high valuation, about 200 times its past year's earnings, which leaves little room for disappointment.
stocks.meaning: AMD has been one of the biggest AI winners of the past year, more than doubling from its low, so it swings hard when sentiment turns. Its own results on Nov. 3 are the next real test of whether AI chip demand is holding up.

outlook.bullCase: Strong Microsoft and Alphabet spending plans on Oct. 28 and solid guidance on Nov. 3 could lift it back toward $560–$600.
outlook.bearCase: If the AI-spending worry deepens, it could slide toward the $470–$480 area where it traded in late September.
outlook.watch: Chip-sector moves, Big Tech capital-spending guidance on Oct. 28–29, and AMD's Nov. 3 results.

stocks.name: American Express
stocks.move: Down about 1–2% in premarket trading Friday after third-quarter results (as of about 8 a.m. ET, per Reuters and GuruFocus)
stocks.why: American Express beat profit forecasts: adjusted earnings were $4.68 a share versus about $4.48 expected, and revenue rose 9% to $20.1 billion, roughly in line. It raised its 2026 adjusted profit forecast to $17.60–$17.90 a share and said it will cut about 5% of its global workforce. Shares still slipped because card spending volumes came in slightly below estimates, with total network volume of $517.9 billion against about $519.5 billion expected.
stocks.meaning: The results show wealthier card users are still spending, especially on travel, which is a decent sign for the consumer economy. But the stock often falls after good reports (Truist notes this would be its ninth drop in 11 quarters after a beat), so expectations were already high.

outlook.bullCase: If investors focus on the raised forecast and cost cuts, the stock could recover and test resistance near $327.
outlook.bearCase: Further worry about slowing spending growth or a weaker consumer, as oil prices squeeze budgets, could keep it under pressure.
outlook.watch: How it trades after the open, U.S. consumer sentiment at 10 a.m. today, and card-spending trends in other lenders' results.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.move: Closed down 3.1% at $374.58 Thursday, near the day's low of $373.71
stocks.why: Tesla rose during the day on Musk's comments that Tesla and SpaceX formed committees to study a merger. After the close it reported adjusted earnings of $0.48 a share versus about $0.45 expected and revenue of $28.05 billion, flat from a year ago and slightly below some forecasts; free cash flow of $1.5 billion beat expectations of a cash burn because spending came in about $3 billion lower than expected. Shares fell about 5% before the open as Tesla cut its 2026 capital-spending plan to about $20 billion from more than $25 billion and Musk said reaching 20,000 Optimus robots a week will take at least a year. Buyers erased the early loss after the open, but it slipped again as the Nasdaq weakened and closed near the day's low.
stocks.meaning: The core business is weak: operating income fell 56% to $718 million and deliveries slipped 2%, so the stock still trades mostly on robotaxi, Optimus and SpaceX-merger hopes. Lower spending helps cash flow but can read as a slower AI push, which explains the early selling.

outlook.bullCase: Concrete merger progress or a smooth Cybercab expansion to Dallas next month could bring it back toward $400–$410.
outlook.bearCase: If the early dip resumes and analysts trim targets, it could slide back toward $355–$375.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds the $374 area, merger committee news, and the NHTSA Cybercab response due Oct. 30.

stocks.name: TD Bank
stocks.move: Closed flat at C$175.14 Thursday after hitting a new 52-week high of C$175.99
stocks.why: Canadian banks have held up while the rest of the market falls. Core inflation measures eased in September even as headline inflation rose to 3.1%, and markets now see about an 80% chance the Bank of Canada raises its rate to 2.50% on Oct. 28. A modest hike tends to help bank lending margins, while lower long-term bond yields this week make bank dividends look more attractive.
stocks.meaning: TD is near a record, so the next leg depends on a stable rate outlook and its next results. Bank stocks are a big part of many Canadian portfolios.

outlook.bullCase: A single, well-signalled hike and calm credit markets could take TD through C$176 to new highs.
outlook.bearCase: A Bank of Canada that signals several hikes, raising fears for mortgage holders and loan losses, could pull it back to the C$167–C$170 area.
